title: JWT verification against JWKS survives a key rotation the realm publishes
asA: operator whose realm rotates its signing keys on the realm's own cadence
iWant: the JWT verifier to recognise a token signed with a new key without a process restart
soThat: a key rotation is transparent to the running project

acceptanceCriteria.description: A verified token whose signing kid is present in the cached JWKS passes verification without a fresh JWKS fetch.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a warm JWKS cache populated by a prior verification against realmSlug='r1' and a new access token signed under the same kid
acceptanceCriteria.then: the verifier consumes the token successfully; no fresh JWKS fetch is observed against the test-injected httpFetch for the duration of this verification; the audit log records no `keycloak.jwks_refreshed` event

acceptanceCriteria.description: A token whose kid is not in the cached JWKS triggers exactly one JWKS refresh; verification succeeds when the refresh surfaces the kid and refuses with `KEYCLOAK_JWT_KID_UNKNOWN` when it does not.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a warm JWKS cache populated by a prior verification and a new access token signed with a kid the realm has rotated to but the cache does not yet carry
acceptanceCriteria.when: the verifier is invoked twice in the same test: once with the realm's fresh JWKS available on the injected httpFetch, once with the httpFetch instrumented to return a JWKS still missing the kid
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first invocation triggers one JWKS refresh (observed on the injected httpFetch), succeeds verification, emits `keycloak.jwks_refreshed`; the second invocation triggers one JWKS refresh, refuses the token with `KEYCLOAK_JWT_KID_UNKNOWN`, emits one `keycloak.jwt_refused` event carrying realmSlug and reason class `kid-unknown`; a third invocation with the same second-token does NOT trigger a further JWKS refresh within the TTL window
